Thanks Rachel — adding the technical clarifications below; pasted for Hutch too.

Short technical summary (for auditor consumption):
- Hosted (Redwood API): fully within Redwood's SOC 2 scope. Controls include centralized identity, RBAC, tenant isolation, and logging retained in our central log cluster for the audit window. We can supply log extracts (auth events, admin/operator actions), change-control tickets, and deployment runbooks.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): considered part of our managed service offering and included in the SOC 2 Type II report when Redwood manages the control plane and node-level operations. For Dedicated we maintain the same access controls and patch/change processes as Hosted. Evidence we can provide: operator access CSV (identity, role, last access), weekly deployment change tickets (Jira IDs), and aggregated KV-cache/noise metrics (sanitized).
- Private / customer-managed VPC or on-prem package: by default out-of-scope for our SOC 2 since customers operate compute and networking. Examples of out-of-scope items: customer-managed firewall rules, customer KMS operations, and on-prem operator accounts. If a customer purchases Redwood-managed Private (where we operate the control plane and manage nodes), we can include that environment in the SOC as an extension — but only if contractual terms confirm operational responsibility and we include it in the auditor's scope.

Caveats and evidence specifics:
- Audit log retention for Hosted/Dedicated: 13 months for primary auth/admin logs, 6 months for detailed application debug traces (we will provide the 13-month extracts covering 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).
- Operator access review: last full review completed 2026-07-20; we can produce the review artifact and the CSV of operator accounts (redacted personal IDs upon request).
- Change management artifacts: we can give Jira export of change tickets for production infra for the audit window (IDs and summary lines; full ticket bodies require an NDA in specific cases).

I'll attach the SOC PDF and a polished bridge letter for you to circulate. Let us know if Hutch requires signatures or notarization.
